newsitem.title: FRANCE: France honours rock, jazz and fashion stars.
newsitem.headline: France honours rock, jazz and fashion stars.

text.p: French rock idol Johnny Hallyday won the Legion of Honour on Wednesday in a New Year's list that also honoured jazz violinist Stephane Grappelli and fashion designer Pierre Cardin.
Hallyday, aged 53 and seen in France as a Gallic answer to Elvis Presley despite scant success abroad, became a chevalier of the Legion of Honour, the lowest rank.
Other entertainers similarly honoured included 63-year-old singer Sacha Distel.
Grappelli, the 88-year-old self-taught grandfather of French jazz violinists, was among those promoted one rank to commander of the Legion of Honour.

Cardin, who has built an empire spanning clothing, food, perfumes, industrial design, real estate and entertainment, was also promoted to commander, third rank on the five-level list published in the Official Journal.
Claudie Andre-Deshays, France's first woman in space who spent 16 days abroad the Mir space station in 1996, was among those who became chevaliers of the Legion of Honour.
Charles Merieux, founder of Merieux medical research laboratories, was the only person awarded the top honour, the Grand Cross of the Legion of Honour.
